note: Start with a C5/C6 split to reveal purity, temperatures and cost before building the product branches.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: establish a sharp C5/C6 split and inspect costs, temperatures and recovery. Step 2: branch the valuable C3-C5 and C6-C9 cuts, using blends where separation is difficult. Step 3: optimize stages/reflux/pressure and prune low-value columns.
Initial feed column: 70 stages, R=B=3, 50% pressure drop, aiming to recover lights including C5 overhead and C6+ in bottoms.

note: Build C5 and C6 blend branches around a sharper C5/C6 feed split; these blends capture most product value without difficult isomer separations.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: establish a sharp C5/C6 split and inspect costs, temperatures and recovery. Step 2: branch the valuable C3-C5 and C6-C9 cuts, using blends where separation is difficult. Step 3: optimize stages/reflux/pressure and prune low-value columns. Now testing three main carbon-number splits simultaneously.
Root at 70/R3 recovered only part of C5 overhead but essentially excluded C6. Increased to 80/R5 for recovery. T targets C5 blend bottoms (~$610M/yr potential); B targets combined C6 blend overhead. Column costs are high (~$235M root), so avoid low-value deep separations unless needed.

note: Switch to a sequential C4/C5, C5/C6, C6/C7 backbone, then split C6 paraffins from naphthenes. This targets the three large blend revenues while discarding only the low-value light cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: establish a C4/C5 root so the discarded light cut is small. Step 2: recover C5 and C6 blends from the bottoms, splitting C7+ first. Step 3: optimize stages/reflux/pressure, then consider C4 and heavy products. Now testing the four-column blend backbone.
My initial C5/C6 root left too much N-butane in the C5 cut and was costly. R82 proved a clean C5 blend via sequential C4/C5 then C5/C6 splits ($375M from a 431 mol/s cut). C6 paraffin blend is the largest opportunity (~$966M if 95%); C6 naphthenes add ~$400M. Discard C3/C4 initially because their blend values may not repay another column.

note: Test a lean two-column C5 blend plant with a warmer C5/C6 root, removing every unsold branch.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: establish a profitable two-column C5 blend core using a warm C5/C6 root followed by C4/C5. Step 2: add only heavy branches whose blend revenue clearly exceeds their cost. Step 3: optimize stages/reflux/pressure and consider C4/heavy products. Now testing the lean C5 core.
Sequential C4/C5 roots are expensive because their cold C4-rich condenser costs $225-350M/yr. A C5/C6 root should have a warmer condenser and still permits a clean C5 blend in the tops branch. R126 gets $403M/yr from C5 but its six columns cost $605M; discard all other branches initially. C6 paraffins are valuable, but n-hexane/methylcyclopentane is a difficult split, so do not pay for it until the core is profitable.

note: Pivot to the much more valuable C6 blends. A low-boil root keeps C6 in the bottoms; the next two columns isolate C6 and split paraffins from naphthenes.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: build a three-column C6-value plant: root C5/C6, then C6/C7, then C6 paraffin/naphthalene split. Step 2: tune the two easy cuts for complete C6 recovery. Step 3: optimize the difficult n-hexane/MCP split and only then add C5/C4 branches.
C6 paraffins plus C6 naphthenes are worth about $1.54B/yr as blends, far more than C5 ($0.59B) or C4 ($0.2B). R173 proved C5 revenue but its full train barely covers costs; discard light products initially. Root reboil controls the cut upward (R173 root boil 2 gave 949 top; R175 boil 3 gave 1508), so boil 1.5 should keep C5 and all C6 in the bottoms. The final split is difficult because n-hexane and MCP boil only 3.1 K apart; use 100 stages and high reflux there.

note: Adopt the proven profitable C6-paraffin plant before pruning its unsold light branch and tuning costs.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R268's proven profitable three-column C6-paraffin backbone. Step 2: tune root/B/T operating costs while preserving 95% C6 purity. Step 3: add or test a C5 recovery branch only if marginal value exceeds cost.
R268 earns $1119M/yr selling 957 mol/s C6 paraffin blend at 96% purity; reward 0.885, cost $731M/yr. Root 70/3/4/0.45 makes a sharp C5/C6 cut; B 110/6/7/0.15 separates C6 from heavies; T 110/6/7 is presently unproductive and costs $184M/yr. Immediate pruning of T may increase reward to about 1.30 without changing the C6 product. Root is the dominant cost and high reflux/boilup columns are expensive, so test pruning before any new branch.

note: Adopt the proven four-column design to secure the C5 blend revenue before optimizing recovery and column costs.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R314's four-column C6-paraffin plus C5-blend plant. Step 2: optimize the cheap TB C4/C5 polisher for recovery and cost. Step 3: reduce root/B/T costs while retaining both blend specifications, then consider further products only if clearly profitable.
R314 is proven at reward 1.716: revenue $1536M/yr, cost $783M/yr. Its BT C6-paraffin blend earns $1119M/yr and TBB C5 blend earns $417M/yr. TB (70/4/3/0.1) costs only $52.5M/yr but leaves 299 mol/s TBT containing 76% C5, so additional C5 recovery may be valuable. Root and B dominate cost at $268M and $279M/yr; T costs $184M/yr. First secure R314, then tune TB and avoid intensifying T, which prior trials showed was costly and ineffective.

note: Adopt R364's lower-boil-up C5 polisher, which improves both C5 recovery and column cost without risking the established C6-paraffin product.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R364's improved four-column C6-paraffin plus C5-blend plant. Step 2: optimize the cheap TB C4/C5 polisher for recovery and cost. Step 3: reduce root/B/T costs while retaining both blend specifications, then consider further products only if clearly profitable.
R364 raises reward to 2.113 by changing TB from 70/4/3/0.1 to 70/6/1.2/0.1. This cuts TB cost from $52.5M to $28.4M/yr and raises C5-blend revenue from $417M to $567M/yr. Root and B still dominate cost at $268M and $279M/yr; T costs $184M/yr. Adopt this proven design first, then test moderate TB settings around it before changing the expensive backbone.

note: Adopt the proven five-column design: the C3/C4 splitter adds a qualifying C4 blend and improves net reward by about $98M/yr.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R407's five-column C6-paraffin, C5-blend and C4-blend plant. Step 2: optimize TT and TB for recovery/cost. Step 3: reduce root/B/T costs while retaining all blend specifications; pursue heavy products only if clearly profitable.
R407 adds TT at 70/4/4/0 to the R364 backbone. TTB qualifies as C4 mix (436 mol/s, 87% N-butane + 13% isobutane), earning $149.3M/yr for $50.9M/yr extra cost, raising reward from 2.113 to 2.337. Root and B dominate cost ($268M and $279M/yr), T costs $184M/yr; TT and TB are much cheaper. Adopt the exact proven design, then test leaner TT settings before backbone changes.

note: Combine R456's cheaper heavy splitter with R458's much cheaper light splitter; their branch results suggest the savings should be additive without losing blend specifications.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: combine the best independent light- and heavy-splitter savings from R456/R458. Step 2: optimize TT/TB and then the expensive root while retaining C4/C5/C6 blend specs. Step 3: consider a saleable heavy branch only after backbone economics are secured.
R456 (2.466) shows B=100/5/6 saves $39.7M/yr and loses only $9.8M revenue. R458 (2.461) shows T=70/4/5 saves $52.3M/yr with slightly higher revenue. These changes are on separate branches, so combining them should give roughly $1109M net, reward ~2.53. B cannot fall to 70/4/5: R460 lost the C6 specification. TT=110/8/4 fails badly by moving propane into C4 bottoms; retain 70/4/4.

note: Test a moderate reduction of the costly C6/heavy splitter; the smaller steps should save energy and size while preserving the narrow C6-blend purity margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 complete: combined best light/heavy savings (2.529). Step 2: optimize the expensive B splitter, then TT/TB and root while retaining C4/C5/C6 specs. Step 3: consider heavy products only if backbone gains stall.
Baseline costs: root 268.2, B 238.8, T 131.9, TT 50.4, TB 28.6 ($M/yr). BT has only ~1% purity margin over the 95% C6-paraffin threshold, so reduce B gradually. B=70/4/5 is known to lose specification (R460). TT=110/8/4 is bad: propane enters C4 bottoms. TBT is only 123 mol/s and TTT is worth at most ~$73M/yr as C3, so extra recovery columns are unlikely to pay.

note: Restore the 2.529 plant and make a smaller C6-splitter reduction; the 90-stage test missed blend purity by only about 1%, so this intermediate setting seeks savings with a safety margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 complete: combined best light/heavy savings (2.529). Step 2: optimize the expensive B splitter in small steps, then TT/TB and root while retaining C4/C5/C6 specs. Step 3: consider heavy products only if backbone gains stall.
Baseline costs: root 268.2, B 238.8, T 131.9, TT 50.4, TB 28.6 ($M/yr). B=90/4.5/5.5 failed C6 spec at 94%; B=70/4/5 also failed. Current test is a cautious 95/4.75/5.5. Heavy recovery train R557 reduced reward; R559's naphthene attempt also failed, so avoid heavy branches. TBT/TTT recovery unlikely to pay.

note: Restore R603 and test three moderate cost reductions: preserve the successful heavy boil-up while lowering its reflux/stages, and trim the two light splitters with product purity margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 complete: combined best light/heavy savings (2.529); R603 now gives 2.561. Step 2: restore R603 and reduce B reflux/stages at the proven boil-up 6, while trimming T and TT; retain C4/C5/C6 specs. Step 3: tune root/TB and only pursue heavy products if backbone gains stall.
R603: root 268.2, B238.8, T118.9, TT50.3, TB28.7. B=95/4.75/5.5 and B=90/4.5/5.5 both lost C6 spec; thus keep boil-up 6. T has purity margin and R603's 60/3.5/4.5 saved $13M. TTB is 100% C4 blend, so TT should tolerate a substantial reduction. Heavy trains have repeatedly underperformed; avoid unless backbone stalls.

note: Adopt R651's profitable TBT recovery, apply the proven TT cost reduction, and add a small butane/C5 polisher on its unsold bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R651 (2.600), trim TT using R652's proven saving, and polish TBTB to recover its C5 blend. Step 2: tune the small recovery columns and TT around product specs. Step 3: only then revisit costly backbone settings.
R651's TBT splitter earns $25M premium butane for $7.7M cost. Its TBTB still contains about 54 mol/s C5 (roughly $48M/yr blend value) contaminated by 19% N-butane; a small second split should be profitable. R652 proves TT=40/2.5/3 saves $13.4M while losing only $2.7M C4 revenue. B=100/5/6 is necessary: 95/4.75/5.5 and 90/4.5/5.5 missed C6 spec. Root and TB are stable; heavy trains underperform.

note: Adopt R698's six-column design: its higher TBT boil-up qualifies the residual C5 blend directly and eliminates the extra polisher, improving both revenue and cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R698 (2.742), whose higher TBT boil-up directly sells both outlets and removes the unprofitable second polisher. Step 2: test modest TBT and light-splitter cost trims while preserving both product specs. Step 3: evaluate whether a small C3 recovery train can beat backbone optimization.
R698 improves on my 2.687 design by $21.3M/yr net: TBT=50/3/4.5 yields 68 mol/s premium N-butane plus 55 mol/s qualifying C5 blend, versus my lower-recovery train. B=100/5/6 remains necessary because 95/4.75/5.5 and 90/4.5/5.5 missed C6 blend purity. TT=40/2.5/3 is the proven low-cost setting. TTT is only 79% C3 and would require both ethane and C4 rejection, so recovery likely needs two columns for at most ~$73M/yr gross.

note: Adopt the profitable C3 recovery train and raise its final splitter's reflux and boil-up to recover some of the substantial C3 still lost in its bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R745 (2.787), whose compact two-column C3 recovery adds net value. Step 2: increase C3 recovery in TTTB while retaining its 95% blend specification. Step 3: use remaining solves for selective low-cost tuning rather than risky backbone changes.
R745 adds $35.3M/yr C3 revenue for $15.1M/yr column cost, beating R698 by 0.045 reward. Its TTTBT is pure C3 but only 138 mol/s, while TTTBB still contains roughly 111 mol/s C3 and is unsold. Increasing TTTB reflux and boil-up from 2.5/3 to 4/4 should recover more of that C3 overhead; the column is small, so even moderate added duty is cheap. B=100/5/6 remains necessary: previous reductions to 95/4.75/5.5 and 90/4.5/5.5 lost C6 blend purity and destroyed most revenue.

note: Adopt R797's best C3 splitter and test a higher boil-up on that small column to recover more C3 from its unsold bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R797 (2.803), currently the best C3 recovery variant. Step 2: extend only its small C3/C4 splitter boil-up to test whether additional recovered C3 outweighs duty. Step 3: reserve remaining solves for selective low-cost tuning; avoid backbone changes.
R797 at TTTB 40/2.5/4.5 earns $43.0M/yr C3, versus $38.2M at 3/4 and $34.0M at 4/4. Its lower reflux and higher boil-up are best. The column costs only $5M/yr, so boil-up 6.0 is a low-risk incremental test. B=100/5/6 must remain: earlier reductions destroyed C6 blend purity and most revenue. Heavy BB and ethane-rich TTTT are not economically separable at this cost level.

note: Boil-up 6.0 still improved C3 recovery profitably, so test 7.5 on the same small splitter to locate the plateau without touching the proven backbone.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: retain the validated 2.814 plant. Step 2: extend only the small C3/C4 splitter boil-up to find the recovery plateau. Step 3: use remaining solves for selective low-cost tuning; avoid backbone changes.
TTTB boil-up 4.5→6.0 raised C3 revenue $43.0→48.2M/yr for only $0.4M/yr extra cost; 5.5 independently confirms the trend. Test 7.5 to see whether useful C3 recovery remains. B=100/5/6 must remain: earlier reductions destroyed C6 blend purity and most revenue. Heavy BB and ethane-rich TTTT are not economically separable at this cost level.

note: Adopt the island-best R888 and test a further heavy-splitter pressure drop to 0.35; dp 0.25 profitably recovered more C6 blend, so check whether that trend continues.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R888 (2.841): B pressure drop 0.25 and TTTB boil-up 8.0. Step 2: test whether higher B pressure drop further improves C6 recovery enough to pay its extra duty. Step 3: retain the best and use remaining solves on selective small-column tuning.
R888 gains $15.4M/yr revenue for $7.3M/yr cost versus my 2.822 plant. B=100/5/6 is essential: 95 stages destroys blend qualification. C3 boil-up 8.0 remains profitable. Now test B dp 0.35; heavy BB and ethane-rich TTTT remain uneconomic.

note: Adopt R934's island-best heavy-column setting and extend its profitable C3 recovery trend to boil-up 10, which added product at negligible cost in R933.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1: adopt R888 (2.841): B pressure drop 0.25 and TTTB boil-up 8.0. Step 2: test whether higher B pressure drop further improves C6 recovery enough to pay its extra duty. Step 3: retain the best and use remaining solves on selective small-column tuning.
R934 shows B dp 0.35 plus C3 boil-up 9.0 reaches 2.857. R933 shows boil-up 10 still adds C3 recovery at negligible cost. Adopt R934 and extend only its small C3 splitter to boil-up 10; preserve the better B dp 0.35.

note: Test two bounded recovery gains: slightly lower B pressure with extra reflux to protect the marginal C6 blend, and higher C3 boil-up to recover propane still left in its tiny bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Preserve the 2.860 design while using the last solves on bounded recovery improvements: approach the heavy-column blend-purity limit with slightly more reflux, and approach complete C3 recovery with higher small-column boil-up. Then retain only validated gains.
B dp 0.40 fails C6 blend purity despite 6 mol/s more tops; dp 0.35 qualifies at 982 mol/s. Test dp 0.36 with reflux 5.1 to offset added naphthene leakage. TTTB boil-up 9->10 recovered 6 mol/s C3 for $0.1M cost and top remains pure; bottoms still contain 29 mol/s propane, so test 15. Avoid further large-column cuts: earlier reductions destroyed the valuable C6 blend.

note: Restore R1014's best heavy-column setting and test C3 boil-up 13; recovery rose profitably through 12, while 15 was past the economic peak.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the island-best R1014 plant, then use the remaining solves to bracket the small C3 splitter's optimum boil-up; keep the delicate heavy C6 cut unchanged.
R1014 scores 2.865 with B=100/5.0/6.0/dp0.35 and TTTB boil-up 12. Boil-up 10->11->12 steadily added saleable C3 at only ~$0.1M/yr extra cost per step; at 15 (tested with a different B) extra duty outweighed recovery. Test 13 to locate the peak. B dp0.40 destroys the C6 blend; dp0.36 with reflux5.1 qualifies but is less profitable than dp0.35/reflux5.0, so do not alter B further.

note: Test the last untried integer C3 boil-up, 14, on the otherwise identical best plant; 13 was still marginally profitable and 15 was past the peak.
notebook:
PLAN: Finish bracketing the small C3 splitter while preserving the validated C6 cut; test boil-up 14, then stop or make only a clearly profitable isolated adjustment.
Best is 2.866 at TTTB boil-up 13. Increments 10->11->12->13 remained profitable, but 15 was too costly in an earlier test. B is extremely sensitive: dp0.40 loses the C6 blend; dp0.36/reflux5.1 qualifies but underperforms dp0.35/reflux5.0, so leave B unchanged. No heavy-products addition is affordable in the remaining solves.

note: Restore the boil-up-13 best and fine-tune the isolated C3 splitter to 13.2; 14 already reduced reward, so only a small interpolation is warranted.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the validated boil-up-13 optimum and use the last solves only for fine interpolation of the cheap C3 splitter; leave every sensitive blend cut unchanged.
Best is 2.866 at TTTB boil-up 13. Integer tests show gains through 13, a small decline at 14, and 15 past the economic peak. Test 13.2 to locate a marginal continuous optimum. B is extremely sensitive: dp0.40 loses the C6 blend and dp0.36/reflux5.1 underperforms dp0.35/reflux5.0, so leave B fixed. No heavy-products addition is affordable.

note: Return to the best boil-up of 13 and test a modest reflux increase on the inexpensive C3 splitter; this may recover additional sellable C3 without disturbing any other stream.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the validated boil-up-13 optimum and use the last solves only on the cheap, isolated C3 splitter; leave every sensitive blend cut unchanged.
Best is 2.866 at TTTB reflux 2.5/boil-up 13. Boil-up 13.2 and 14 are slightly worse, and 15 is past the economic peak. Test reflux 2.7 at boil-up 13: extra rectification may recover more C3 into the qualifying tops for little cost. B is extremely sensitive: dp0.40 loses the C6 blend and dp0.36/reflux5.1 underperforms dp0.35/reflux5.0, so leave B fixed. No heavy-products addition is affordable.

note: Restore the proven optimum and make one final capital-saving test on the small C3 splitter: five fewer stages may preserve most recovery while reducing cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the validated boil-up-13 optimum and use the last solves only on the cheap, isolated C3 splitter; leave every sensitive blend cut unchanged.
Best is R1049 at 2.866 with TTTB 40 stages, reflux 2.5, boil-up 13. Boil-up 13.2 and 14 are slightly worse, 15 is past the peak, and reflux 2.7 is worse. Final test: 35 stages at the optimum ratios; modestly lower capital may retain enough C3 recovery. B is extremely sensitive: dp0.40 loses the C6 blend and dp0.36/reflux5.1 underperforms dp0.35/reflux5.0, so leave B fixed. No heavy-products addition is affordable.

note: Use the last solve to test 30 stages on the inexpensive C3 splitter; 35 stages preserved recovery, so a further capital reduction may add a small final gain.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the final solve on the isolated C3 splitter's stage count; retain the validated boil-up-13 design if this last capital-saving test underperforms.
R1049 at 2.866 uses TTTB 40 stages, reflux 2.5, boil-up 13. Boil-up 13.2/14 and reflux 2.7 are slightly worse; 15 is past the peak. Reducing to 35 stages preserved the displayed revenue and reward while trimming cost slightly. Final test: 30 stages, leaving all other columns unchanged. B is highly sensitive (dp0.40 loses the C6 blend; dp0.36/reflux5.1 is worse), so keep B at dp0.35/reflux5.0. No heavy-products addition is affordable.
